wave: CORRECTNESS -- the engineering-graph projection silently dropped R4.12's CALL argument/result data-flow bindings, unlike its structurally identical PERSISTENCE sibling
wave_title: Third fix this generation cycle after returning to the top of the standing priority order (correctness/architectural integrity, then security). Two prior rounds this cycle scoped their surveys to adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs (a version-mismatch bug, then a path-traversal bug); this round deliberately scoped a fresh Explore survey AWAY from that file to avoid re-treading already-scrutinized ground, into core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs's SemanticObservation-to-Edge projection instead.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. A real, silent, total loss of a documented R4.12 fact class (call argument/result data-flow bindings) between census and the produced engineering graph -- the exact kind of census-to-graph fidelity gap R5's own invariants (GRAPH_BEFORE_CODE, NORMALIZATION_MUST_NOT_DROP_CENSUS_FACTS) exist to prevent.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped away from the file two prior rounds this cycle had already scrutinized (adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs), into core/src/graph, runtime/src/census, core/src/language/adl, and apps/cli/src/main.rs instead. Its single reported candidate was independently re-verified before any change: read core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs's SemanticObservation::Call arm (lines 570-605) and its structurally analogous SemanticObservation::Persistence arm (lines 1006-1071) directly, and read core/src/semantic/call.rs's CallSiteIdentity struct definition (lines 51-82) to confirm `arguments: Vec<PlaceRef>` and `result: PlaceRef` are real, already-populated R4.12 fields, not aspirational/unused ones.
key_finding: CallSiteIdentity.arguments (one PlaceRef per syntactic argument position) and .result (a PlaceRef to the DATA_FLOW value a call's return directly becomes) are real, documented R4.12 fields the Rust extractor's own build_calls path genuinely populates with PlaceRef::Resolved when it can prove a simple binding (e.g. `let y = helper(x);`). The graph projection's Call arm in build_system_graph only ever read header.subject.function (the caller) to emit the CallSite node and MAKES_CALL edge -- it never read arguments or result at all. This is a genuine drift between two structurally identical code paths added in the same R4.11/R4.12 generation: PERSISTENCE's own `place: PlaceRef` field IS projected (via the existing `place_node_id_for` helper, drawing a REFERS_TO_PLACE edge to DATA_FLOW's already-existing node when Resolved), but CALL's arguments/result PlaceRefs, using the exact same type and the exact same convergence pattern, were never wired up -- a silent, total drop of this fact class from every produced engineering graph.
verification_before_acting: Read the real, current Call and Persistence arms directly (not from the subagent's paraphrase) to confirm the exact asymmetry: Persistence calls place_node_id_for on a Resolved place; Call never touches arguments/result at all.

Read CallSiteIdentity's own doc comments in core/src/semantic/call.rs, which explicitly document arguments/result as R4.12 facts computed via `ValueIdentity::identity_key()` the same way DATA_FLOW's own walker computes its record_ids -- confirming the record_id a Resolved PlaceRef carries genuinely points at a real, already-producible DATA_FLOW node, making place_node_id_for directly reusable with no new lookup logic needed.

Checked the existing call_observation test helper (used by three existing Call tests) and confirmed it hardcodes arguments: Vec::new() and result: PlaceRef::Unresolved unconditionally -- no existing graph test exercises a Resolved argument or result for Call, confirming this was a genuine, previously-uncovered gap.

design_decisions.question: What edge kind(s) and shape should argument/result bindings use?
design_decisions.decision: Two new kinds, BINDS_ARGUMENT (one edge per Resolved argument position, from the CallSite node to the DATA_FLOW place node, with a "position" attribute recording the 0-indexed syntactic argument position) and BINDS_RESULT (one edge from the CallSite node to the DATA_FLOW place node, when Resolved). Kept the two semantically distinct rather than reusing PERSISTENCE's REFERS_TO_PLACE, since "this call's Nth argument binds to this value" and "this call's result becomes this value" are different relationships a graph consumer needs to tell apart, and only BINDS_ARGUMENT needs a position; this also matches this file's own existing convention of one distinct edge kind per distinct relationship (MAKES_CALL, PRODUCES_PERSISTENCE_OP, REFERS_TO_PLACE, HAS_VALUE, ... are all separately named).

design_decisions.question: Reuse the existing place_node_id_for helper, or write new lookup logic?
design_decisions.decision: Reuse place_node_id_for(dimension, record_id) unchanged -- it already exists precisely to convert a Resolved PlaceRef into the correct existing node id for any SemanticDimension, is already proven correct by PERSISTENCE's own tests, and CALL's arguments/result carry the exact same PlaceRef shape.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The engineering-graph projection now projects every Resolved CALL argument/result PlaceRef into a BINDS_ARGUMENT/BINDS_RESULT edge pointing at the SAME DATA_FLOW node that dimension's own observation produced, closing a silent total-drop gap; an Unresolved argument/result correctly still produces no edge, exactly like PERSISTENCE's own Unresolved case.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added a new call_observation_with_bindings test helper (call_observation itself always hardcodes empty/Unresolved, so it cannot exercise this path) plus two new tests: an_unresolved_call_never_produces_a_binds_argument_or_binds_result_edge (regression guard using the existing helper) and resolved_call_argument_and_result_converge_on_the_existing_data_flow_nodes (the real fix, modeled directly on the already-proven resolved_persistence_place_converges_on_the_existing_state_access_node pattern -- constructs a real DATA_FLOW value observation, a Call observation whose argument/result PlaceRefs resolve to that value's own record_id, and asserts the resulting BINDS_ARGUMENT/BINDS_RESULT edges target the exact node id DATA_FLOW's own observation produced).
